Read the 1 per cent column first, and notice how flat it is. The one-in-a-hundred bad run costs 19.2 per cent and needs 23.8 per cent to undo — four and a half points more than it took, which is an annoyance. Now read the 3 per cent column. The same one-in-a-hundred run costs 48.5 per cent and needs 94.1 per cent, which is not an annoyance and is barely a plan. The market delivered one distribution of R into both columns. Everything that differs between them is the fraction, and you chose the fraction before any of this began.
